t: What happens when I attack?
a:
To attack, move your units to a battlefield where your opponent has units. A standard move exhausts the unit and can only be done on your own turn in your Main Phase (not during a showdown or combat): base to a battlefield or back, or battlefield to battlefield only with Ganking. That battlefield becomes contested and combat starts at the next cleanup.
1) Combat showdown: you are the Attacker, their units there are Defenders. "When I attack / defend" abilities trigger (yours first). You get focus first, then you take turns playing [Action] and [Reaction] cards until both pass.
2) Damage: each side adds up its units' Might (Assault adds Might to attackers, Shield to defenders; stunned units deal no combat damage). You assign your damage first, then they do: each unit must get lethal damage in full before the next one gets any, Tank units first, Backline units last. All damage lands at once.
3) Result: units with lethal damage (at least 1 and at least their Might) die, then every unit heals. If any defender is still alive, your attackers are sent back to base. If only your units are left you take control of the battlefield, which is a conquer worth 1 point if you haven't scored it this turn.
Moving into an empty enemy battlefield is a showdown instead of a combat: if your units are still there when it ends, you take it.

t: How do I score points?
a:
Two ways, each 1 point: Conquer, which is taking control of a battlefield you haven't scored this turn, and Hold, which is still controlling a battlefield in your Beginning Phase. Each battlefield can score you only once per turn, by either method.
The final point is special: if you're 1 point from winning, a conquer only gives that last point if you've scored every battlefield this turn; otherwise you draw a card instead. Points from holding or from card effects don't have that limit.
Card text that says "score 1 point" (or gain points) just gives you points: it isn't a conquer or a hold, doesn't use up a battlefield's score for the turn, and isn't limited by the final-point rule (CR 470.2, 473.1.a.1).

t: How do I win?
a: In a 1v1 duel you win when you have at least 8 points and more points than your opponent. It's checked at every cleanup, so it happens the moment it's true. Remember the final-point rule: the conquer that would take you to 8 only counts if you've scored every battlefield this turn (otherwise you draw a card), but a hold or a card effect can give the 8th point normally. If your deck runs out you Burn Out, which gives your opponent a point. If both players are at 8 or more with the same score, nobody has won yet: play continues until one of you is ahead (CR 323.1, 474).

t: How does a game start?
a: Each player puts their legend in the legend zone and their Chosen Champion in the champion zone, sets aside their battlefields (in a duel one of each player's battlefields is used), and shuffles both decks. The first player is decided at random. Each player draws 4 cards, then mulligans in turn order. The player who goes second channels 1 extra rune in their first Channel Phase.

t: How does the mulligan work?
a: After drawing your opening 4, in turn order each player may set aside up to 2 cards, draw that many, then put the set-aside cards on the bottom of the Main Deck. Then the first player takes the first turn.

t: What happens in a turn?
a: Awaken: ready everything you control. Beginning: start-of-turn effects (Temporary units die), then you score a Hold for every battlefield you control. Channel: put 2 runes from your rune deck onto the board. Draw: draw 1 (from an empty deck you Burn Out first). Main: your rune pool empties, then you play cards, use abilities and move units. Ending: end-of-turn effects, then all units heal, "this turn" effects end and rune pools empty.

t: How do runes, energy and power work?
a: Each rune can either be exhausted for 1 energy or recycled (put on the bottom of your rune deck) for 1 power of its color. Both can be done at Reaction speed when you need to pay. You channel 2 runes a turn. Recycling a rune for power takes it off the board, so power can also come from Seals or Gold, which keeps your runes. Your rune pool empties at the start of your Main Phase and at the end of each turn, so unspent energy and power are lost.

t: Can I play cards on my opponent's turn?
a: Normally you can only play cards in your own Main Phase, when nothing else is happening. [Action] cards can also be played during showdowns and combats, on anyone's turn. [Reaction] cards can do all that plus be played while something is on the chain, which means in response to another card. Hidden cards gain [Reaction] from the turn after you hide them.

t: If we both play cards, which happens first?
a: Cards and abilities go on the chain. While a chain exists only [Reaction] cards can be added. When everyone passes in a row, the newest item resolves first, then players can respond again before the next one. So the last thing played resolves first. Units, gear and resource-adding abilities resolve as soon as they finish being played and can't be responded to. If a spell's target is gone or no longer legal when it resolves, that part is skipped. You can respond to a response: if they counter your spell, you can counter their counter (a counter war), and again the newest card resolves first. Last in, first out: the first card played is the last to resolve. In combat, the attacker's "when I attack" triggers go on the chain first and the defender's "when I defend" triggers go on last, so the defender's resolve first; each player orders their own. After each item resolves, units with lethal damage die (together) before the next item resolves, and a trigger still resolves even if its unit has died.

t: What happens when my unit dies?
a: A unit has lethal damage when it has at least 1 damage and at least as much damage as its Might. At the next cleanup its Deathknell / "when I die" abilities trigger, then it dies and goes to its owner's trash. A token stops existing when it leaves the board. Damage that isn't lethal heals at the end of each turn and after each combat. If the death is replaced (for example the unit is recalled instead), its Deathknell doesn't trigger. Deathknell and other "when I leave the board" abilities are checked just before the unit leaves; if something saves it instead (Guardian Angel, Tactical Retreat, a recall), it never left, so they don't trigger (CR 383.2.c.3).

t: When do units heal?
a: All units heal at the end of every turn and after each combat, so damage only matters if it's lethal right away (at least 1 and at least the unit's Might).

t: What if both sides have the same Might?
a: Combat damage is dealt at the same time, so units can trade. Each side deals damage equal to its total Might. With equal Might, each side can usually give the other lethal damage, so both die. If both sides are wiped out, nobody gets a result and nobody gains control there. If any defender survives, the attackers are sent back to base and there's no result. If only one side has units left, that side wins the combat and controls the battlefield.

t: What is Hidden?
a: On your turn, when nothing is happening, you can pay 1 power of any color to put a Hidden card facedown at a battlefield you control that has no facedown card. From your next turn it has [Reaction] and can be played for free while you still control that battlefield. A hidden unit or gear is played to that battlefield, and a hidden spell's targets must be there. If you lose control of the battlefield, the hidden card is removed. You can always just play it from your hand for its normal cost instead.

t: What is a showdown?
a: A showdown starts when a battlefield becomes contested, for example when you move onto it. The player who contested it gets focus first. With focus you can play an [Action] or [Reaction] card, or pass; focus then goes to the other player. When everyone passes in a row it ends. In a combat it moves on to damage. In a showdown with no enemy units, the player still there takes control, which is a conquer if they haven't scored it this turn.

t: What do Tank and Backline do?
a: When the enemy assigns combat damage, your Tank units must be given lethal damage before any of your non-Tank units. Backline units are given damage only after all your non-Backline units have lethal damage. Shield and Assault don't change this order; they only add Might.

t: What do Shield and Assault do?
a: Shield X gives the unit +X Might while it's defending. Assault X gives +X Might while it's attacking. A blank value means 1, and several values add up.

t: What does Stun do?
a: A stunned unit deals no combat damage (its Might counts as 0 for combat damage). It can still be damaged and killed.

t: What does Deflect do?
a: Deflect X: your opponent's spells and abilities that choose this unit cost X more power, of any color, for each time they choose it. A blank value means 1, and values add up. It's a mandatory extra cost for them.

t: What does Accelerate do?
a: When you play a unit with Accelerate you may pay 1 extra energy plus 1 power of one of its colors. If you do, it enters the board READY instead of exhausted, so it can act that turn. It doesn't "become ready", so ready-triggers don't fire. It can't be paid after the unit is on the board.

t: Why can't my new unit move?
a: Units enter the board exhausted, unless they have Accelerate (paid) or an effect readies them. A standard move exhausts the unit, so an exhausted unit can't move until your next Awaken, when everything you control readies. Gear enters ready.

t: What happens if my deck runs out?
a: If you have to draw (or take) more cards than your Main Deck has, you Burn Out: you draw what you can, shuffle your trash in as your new deck, your opponent gains 1 point, then you finish drawing. Look, reveal and predict never cause a burn out. When your opponent burns out, you gain that point. If a player keeps burning out (the new deck is empty too), an opponent gains a point each time, and those points can win the game (CR 432.2, 432.3).

t: How does Equipment work?
a: Equipment is gear that attaches to a unit you control. Equip [cost] is an ability: pay it to attach the gear (the unit is a target), and the unit is then "equipped". Quick-Draw Equipment has [Reaction] and attaches itself to one of your units when you play it. Weaponmaster: when you play that unit, you may attach one of your Equipment to it, paying its Equip cost minus 1 power, even outside normal timing. Equipment moves with its unit, and that doesn't count as a move. Gear left at a battlefield (for example after the unit it was attached to dies there) goes back to your base at the next cleanup.

t: How do moving and recalling work?
a: A standard move (exhaust, your Main Phase, not during a showdown or combat) takes a unit from base to a battlefield or back. Ganking also allows battlefield to battlefield. You can move a group together if they go to the same place. Moves are instant and can't be responded to. A recall sends a unit to base without moving, so "when I move" doesn't trigger and it keeps its damage.

t: When do I lose control of a battlefield?
a: You keep a battlefield while you have units there. If you have no units at a battlefield you control, you lose control of it at the next cleanup (when no showdown or combat is happening there). A unit with 0 Might can still take an empty battlefield and hold it, because Might doesn't decide control.

t: What does counter mean?
a: Countering cancels a card or ability on the chain. A countered card goes to the trash, its costs aren't refunded, and it never counts as played.

t: What are the deck-building rules?
a: 1 Champion Legend (its two colors are your Domain Identity), a Main Deck of at least 40 cards including your Chosen Champion, a Rune Deck of exactly 12 runes, and 3 battlefields for a duel (no two with the same name). Up to 3 copies of any card name, and at most 3 Signature cards in total. Every card must fit your legend's colors, and banned cards aren't allowed. A card with no domain (colorless) can go in a deck of any colors (CR 103.2.b.5).

t: Which cards are banned?
a: From Nov 23, 2026: Riven, Broken Blade; Zhonya's Hourglass; Stellacorn Herder; Nocturne, Horrifying; Rhasa the Sunderer; Brynhir Thundersong; Dazzling Aurora; Baited Hook. Battlefields: Emperor's Dais and Star Spring.

t: What are Flow and Repeat?
a: Flow [cost]: you may play the spell from your trash for its Flow cost, with the same timing as normal; then it's banished instead of going back to the trash. Repeat [cost]: an optional extra cost; if you pay it, the spell's effect happens one more time, and you can make new choices for the repeat. It still counts as played once.

t: What do Legion, Temporary, Deathknell and Ambush mean?
a: Legion: the text after it works only if you've already played another card this turn. Temporary: the unit dies at the start of your Beginning Phase, before scoring, so it can't score a hold. Deathknell: "when I die", which only triggers if it actually goes to the trash. Ambush: the unit can be played to a battlefield where you have units, and has [Reaction] there, so it can come down mid-combat.

t: Angler Wyrm, Charm and other "move an enemy unit" effects
a: Angler Wyrm: exhaust it and choose an opponent; THEY pick one of their units and move it to the Wyrm's battlefield. A move made by an effect doesn't exhaust the unit and isn't a standard move, so it can happen outside their turn and needs no Ganking. Their unit arriving makes your battlefield contested, so a combat starts at the next cleanup. Their unit is the attacker and it fights ALL of your units there, not just the Wyrm: damage is assigned as usual (Tank first, Backline last). If your units survive, their unit dies or is sent back to base and you keep the battlefield. If only their unit is left, they take control of it, which counts as a conquer for them. They will usually pick the unit most likely to win, or the one they mind losing least. Charm, Evelynn, Entrancing and Irresistible Faefolk work the same way when they pull an enemy unit to a battlefield where you have units.

t: What happens when a Bomb blows up?
a:
Short answer: when a Bomb goes away by dying ("blowing up"), its Deathknell deals 2 damage to one enemy unit at that battlefield, and it kills your other Bombs there, which each deal 2 more. If a Bomb goes away without dying (banished or returned to a hand), nothing happens: it's a token, so it simply stops existing and no damage is dealt.
A Bomb is a gear token. Like every token it costs nothing, has no color, and simply stops existing when it leaves the board (it never goes to your trash). It has Deploy, so it is always put at a battlefield, never in your base.
A Bomb "blows up" when it dies. That happens when your opponent holds that battlefield (Deploy: when an opponent holds here, kill this; that's at the start of their turn when they score it), or when a card kills it: one of yours (Ziggs, Explosive when he defends, Hexplosive Minefield, Brittle Steel, Detonation Amplifier, Mordekaiser) or one of theirs (any "kill a gear" effect).
When it dies, its Deathknell happens: you deal 2 damage to ONE enemy unit at that battlefield (you choose which; to choose a unit with Deflect you must pay one power of any color), and ALL your other Bombs at that same battlefield die too. Each of those has its own Deathknell, so each deals another 2 to an enemy unit there (the same one or a different one). Three Bombs at one battlefield = three hits of 2.
Bonuses: with Ziggs, Short-Fused on the board each Bomb hit deals 3. Detonation Amplifier at that battlefield, or Karthus, Eternal on your board, makes each Bomb's Deathknell happen an extra time (two hits per Bomb).
If there are no enemy units at that battlefield, the hits do nothing, but the Bombs are still gone. Damage that reaches a unit's Might kills it; other damage heals at the end of the turn.
r: Bomb token text, Deploy, Deathknell, 182-187 tokens, 428

t: What is a Gold token?
a:
Gold is a gear token in your base. Its ability: kill this, exhaust it: add 1 power of any color. It works at Reaction speed, so you can use it on any turn, even while paying for a card, and adding resources can't be responded to.
Gold gives power, not energy. Many cards make Gold "exhausted": exhausted Gold can't be used until it readies at the start of your next turn. Gold made ready can be used right away.
Using Gold for power instead of recycling a rune keeps your runes on the board, so spend Gold first. It's a token, so once used it's gone.

t: What are tokens (Recruit, Sprite, Mech, Sand Soldier, Bird)?
a:
Tokens are units or gear made by card effects. The player who made it controls it. Tokens cost 0, have no color, and stop existing the moment they leave the board: a token returned to hand, killed or banished is just gone.
The common ones: Recruit (1 Might), Bird (1 Might with Deflect), Tentacle (1 Might), Sand Soldier (2 Might), Mech (3 Might), Sprite (3 Might with Temporary: it dies at the start of your next turn before you score), Reflection (copies another unit), Shadow Clone (0 Might; when it attacks you may banish a unit from your trash to give it Assault 4), plus the Gold and Bomb gear tokens.
Apart from that a token unit is a normal unit: it enters exhausted unless the card says ready, it can attack, defend, hold and conquer, and it can be buffed or equipped.

t: What does Buff do?
a:
To buff a unit, put a buff counter on it: it has +1 Might for as long as it stays on the board. A unit can have only one buff at a time; buffing a unit that already has one does nothing (it is still a legal choice).
Some cards let you spend a buff as a cost: remove a buff counter from one of your own units. Buffs are lost when the unit leaves the board.

t: What are Empower and Empowered?
a:
Empower [cost] is an ability: pay the cost to give the card the Empowered status. You can only use it if it isn't already Empowered (Kayle, Justified is the exception: she can be Empowered up to three times).
Text after [Empowered] only works while the card is Empowered, and "when I become Empowered" triggers at that moment. Some cards Empower or disempower other things (Profiteer, Ambessa's legend). A unit that leaves the board loses its Empowered status.

t: How do XP, Hunt and Level work?
a:
XP is a resource you, the player, collect (it isn't on a card and has no limit). Hunt X: when that unit conquers or holds, you gain X XP. Several Hunt numbers add up.
Level N: the text after it works while you have N or more XP, and switches off as soon as you drop below N (some cards spend XP). Level counts the XP of the card's current controller.

t: What do Deploy and Ganking mean?
a:
Deploy (on gear): you can only play it to a battlefield, never your base. When an opponent holds that battlefield (scores it at the start of their turn), the gear is killed. Demacian Standard, The Ball, The Good Stuff, Pillaged Armory and Bombs all have Deploy.
Ganking (on units): the unit's normal move can also go straight from one battlefield to another. Without Ganking a unit must go battlefield → base → battlefield.

t: What do Vision, Predict and Burn mean?
a:
Predict: look at the top card of your Main Deck and choose whether to recycle it (put it on the bottom). Predict X: do that X times. Predicting never makes you burn out.
Vision: when you play this card, Predict once.
Burn X: that player puts the top X cards of their Main Deck into their trash. If the deck runs out while doing it, they burn out (see "What happens if my deck runs out?").

t: What do Show Off, Mighty, Unique, Disarm and Legion mean?
a:
Show Off [something]: as you play the card, you may reveal a matching card from your hand or pick a matching friendly card on the board, to get the card's bonus.
Mighty: a unit is Mighty while it has 5 or more Might. "Becomes Mighty" means it just went from under 5 to 5 or more.
Unique: your deck can have only 1 card with that name.
Disarm X: when this unit attacks, give an enemy unit at that battlefield -X Might this turn.
Legion: the text after it works only if you've already played another card this turn.

t: What is the difference between kill, discard, banish and recycle?
a:
Kill: a unit or gear goes from the board to its owner's trash, and its Deathknell triggers. Lethal damage kills too.
Discard: a card goes from your hand to your trash.
Banish: the card goes to the banishment zone. That is not a kill, so Deathknell does not trigger, and cards in banishment are out of the game unless a card brings them back.
Recycle: put cards on the BOTTOM of their deck (several at once in random order). Tokens that would go to any of these places just stop existing.

t: How do my legend and chosen champion work?
a:
Your legend stays in its own zone the whole game. It isn't a unit, can't be attacked, killed or moved, and gives you abilities (usually by exhausting it; it readies at the start of your turn).
Your chosen champion starts in the champion zone, and you can play it from there whenever you could play it from your hand, paying its cost. Once it leaves the champion zone it can't normally go back. Other copies with the same name count as your chosen champion too.

t: Can I use runes, Gold or Seals at any time?
a:
Abilities that add energy or power (exhausting or recycling a rune, Gold, Seals) work at Reaction speed and can't be responded to. You can use them in the middle of paying for a card.
Unspent energy and power empty from your pool at the end of each turn, so only add what you need.

t: What happens when things happen at the same time?
k: deal damage at the same time
a:
Short answer: damage in a fight is dealt at the same time, everything that took lethal damage dies together, and when both players have triggers at the same time the turn player's go on the chain first, so the other player's resolve first.
Combat damage: each side totals its Might and assigns it (the attacker assigns first, but nothing happens until both have assigned), then all of it is dealt at once. A unit that dies still deals its damage.
Dying together: at the next cleanup every unit with lethal damage dies at the same moment. Their Deathknells all trigger, but the dying units have already left the board when those Deathknells resolve, so a Deathknell can only choose a unit that survived.
Order: if one player has several triggers at once, that player picks their order. If both players do, the turn player puts all of theirs on the chain first and the other player puts theirs on top; the chain resolves newest first, so the non-turn player's triggers resolve first. In a normal attack that means the defender's Deathknells resolve before the attacker's.
"Alone" and "when another unit dies" checks look at the moment of death: a friend dying at the same moment still counts as being there (Lonely Poro does not draw), and a unit that dies at the same time as another doesn't see that death (Pyke dying alongside an enemy unit makes no Gold).
Damage prevention or "would die" effects (Zhonya's Hourglass, Guardian Angel): because the units die together, you choose which of your dying units such an effect saves.
Bombs: several of your Bombs at one battlefield die together, and each Bomb's Deathknell hits for 2.

t: What if a unit's Might goes below 0?
a: A unit's Might can go below 0 (for example from Disarm or a -Might effect), but anything that looks at its Might treats it as 0, and so does combat: a unit at -2 adds 0 to its side's damage, not -2 (CR 143.2.c). Its real value still counts for later math, so a +3 on a unit at -2 Might leaves it at 1. A 0-Might unit can't be killed by 0 damage: lethal damage is always at least 1.

t: When can I use a unit's or gear's ability?
a: Abilities written as "cost: effect" (for example "[1], [Exhaust]: deal 1...") are activated abilities. You can use them only in your own Main Phase when nothing else is happening: not during a showdown, a combat, or while something is on the chain, unless the ability has [Action] (then also in showdowns and combats) or [Reaction] (then any time, even in response) (CR 381). Abilities that start with "When" or "At" (and Deathknell) aren't used by you: they trigger by themselves, on anyone's turn. Abilities that add energy or power (runes, Gold, Seals) can be used whenever you need to pay (CR 357.1.a).

t: Is "deal 1 for each..." one hit or several?
a: One hit. "Deal X for each ..." adds everything up and deals it as a single instance of damage, so Bonus Damage or anything that cares about "each time damage is dealt" applies once (CR 418.8). Bonus Damage is added once per deal; if a spell deals damage to several units, each target gets the bonus.

t: What happens when Orianna's legend animates a gear (The Ball)?
a: Orianna, Lady of Clockwork: at the start of your Main Phase you may pay [1] to choose a friendly gear, in your base or at a battlefield (a deployed The Ball counts). It becomes a unit gear with Might equal to its Energy cost (The Ball: 5) and stays a unit until you choose another gear. Becoming a unit isn't a move, so The Ball's "when you play or move this" doesn't trigger then. If it's at a battlefield you don't control, it contests it: a showdown if no enemy units are there (you can conquer), or a fight with it as the attacker if there are. As a unit, The Ball has Ganking (it can move from battlefield to battlefield), and every time it moves you choose: draw 1 or deal 2 to enemy units there. It's still a gear (it counts for Patched Porobot and lets Orianna, Exquisite deal combat damage); if it's returned to hand or killed, The Ball card goes to your hand or trash.
r: Orianna, Lady of Clockwork; The Ball; CR 323.10.a, 446

t: How do Tornado Warrior and Steel Paws work together?
a: Tornado Warrior: when you play it from face down (Hidden), you may empower something at that battlefield, and it is disempowered at the end of the turn. Steel Paws has Empower [7] and +7 Might while Empowered, so flipping Tornado Warrior next to Steel Paws makes Paws a 7 for that turn without paying 7. It must be played from face down (a normal play does nothing) and only empowers something at the same battlefield. If you already paid to empower Steel Paws, Tornado Warrior adds nothing and Paws stays empowered.

t: Can Charm stop my opponent from scoring a hold?
a: Yes, often. Charm has no [Action] or [Reaction], so you can only play it in your own main phase with the Chain empty. Holds are scored at the start of your opponent's turn, before they can move. If their only unit at a battlefield they control is moved away (to their base), they no longer have a unit there, lose control, and score no hold there next turn. Charm can't choose a unit with Deflect unless you pay the extra cost, and can't choose a unit that can't be chosen (like Ruin Runner).

t: How does Alpha Strike's damage work?
a: Alpha Strike ([Action]): choose a friendly unit; it deals damage equal to its Might, split however you like among enemy units at battlefields (not in base). Then you gain 1 XP for each unit that damage killed. It counts as damage from that unit, chosen by a spell, so units with Deflect cost extra to choose and units that can't be chosen are skipped. All units it kills die together in one cleanup.

t: How much does Sky Splitter cost?
k: cost is reduced by the highest might
a: Sky Splitter costs 8 Energy minus the highest Might among units you control right now (never below 0), then deals 5 to a unit at a battlefield. With a 6-Might unit it costs 2; with no units it costs the full 8. Power costs are not reduced.

t: Does Thrill of the Hunt keep my unit's buffs and damage?
a: No. Thrill of the Hunt ([Reaction]) banishes your unit, then you play it to any battlefield without paying its cost. It comes back as a new object: damage, buffs, 'this turn' bonuses and attached equipment are gone, and 'when you play me' effects happen again. It is played, not moved, so 'when I move' effects don't trigger. During a showdown it joins that fight.
